rows.reviewed_claim_types: CP1 typed rho/rho_tw antiholomorphic real-structure maps, vector vs projective squares, no real fixed points, real conic
rows.predecessor_obligation: W05 defines a real structure on CP1 as an antiholomorphic map rho: CP1 -> CP1 with rho squared equal to 1. The ordinary real structure is complex conjugation rho([z1,z2])=[bar(z1),bar(z2)]; its real points are exactly the points fixed by rho, forming a circle in CP1 (the real line in the affine z coordinate). W05 explicitly contrasts this ordinary real structure with the twistor antipodal real structure rho_tw, defined by rho_tw([z1,z2])=[-bar(z2),bar(z1)] (equivalently rho_tw(z)=-1/bar(z)); on C2 coordinates rho_tw squared equals -1, while on projective points rho_tw squared equals 1, and on the sphere rho_tw is the antipodal map with no projective fixed points. W05 also presents the same twistor P1 as the real projective conic x^2+y^2+z^2=0 in projective two-space, defined over the real numbers, with complex points but no real points. W05 explicitly identifies the Riemann sphere CP1 with complex lines in C2: homogeneous [z1,z2] denotes an equivalence class of pairs of complex numbers, and the affine coordinate chart z=z1/z2 identifies C with CP1 minus the point [z1,0]. For ordinary conjugation W05 also gives rho(z)=bar(z) in this affine chart. For the twistor map, W05 explicitly shows that the fixed-point equation z=-1/bar(z) would imply |z|^2=-1, a contradiction for a complex number. W05 furthermore describes the twistor P1 as the complex projective variety CP1 equipped with an action of Gal(C/R) and separately as the equation-defined real projective conic; these are its two source-given presentations. W05 writes the ordinary homogeneous real-point fixed-point equation rho([z1,z2])=[z1,z2] as the criterion for a real point of the ordinary structure. W05 also explicitly states that no projective point satisfies the homogeneous twistor fixed-point equation rho_tw([z1,z2])=[z1,z2]; this equation occurs under the source's negated existence claim, not as an asserted positive fixed point. In this W05 §2 source statement, rho_tw is itself the declared antiholomorphic CP1 real-structure MAP with source-given homogeneous arguments and outputs, not an optional relation restricted to witnessed two-step applications. Its map-type CP1 domain/codomain, projective-square identity, and projective fixed-point nonexistence are separate source obligations; the coordinate-level square-minus-identity and affine formula are distinct carrier/chart clauses and do not replace the projective type law.

rows.reviewed_claim_types: ordinary/twistor CP3 maps, HP1=S4 quotient, left inverse q2, pi:CP3→HP1 and invariant CP1 fibers
rows.predecessor_obligation: W05 states that rho_tw on CP3 has no fixed projective points but has a four-real-dimensional family of invariant CP1 real lines parametrized by HP1=S4; each such line is a twistor P1.  W05 identifies PT=CP3 as complex lines in T=C4=H2 and explicitly gives the ordinary CP3 map rho([z1,z2,z3,z4])=[bar(z1),bar(z2),bar(z3),bar(z4)] and twistor map rho_tw([z1,z2,z3,z4])=[-bar(z2),bar(z1),-bar(z4),bar(z3)]. Ordinary rho has real-point space RP3 of real dimension three; rho_tw has no real points but preserves a four-real-dimensional family of projective CP1 lines that are real lines. W05 presents HP1=S4 through quaternion pairs [q1,q2] as homogeneous equivalence classes, with affine ordered quotient q=(q2)^-1 q1 identifying H with HP1 minus [q1,0]. The explicit map pi:[z1,z2,z3,z4] in CP3 -> [z1+z2j,z3+z4j] in HP1 takes each complex line to its generated quaternionic line; its fibers are exactly the CP1 real lines for rho_tw. Each fiber is a twistor P1 on which the restricted rho_tw acts as in W05 §2.

rows.reviewed_claim_types: SL2C vs SL2H actions do not commute with real structure, Euclidean PT vs Minkowski PT* and chirality
rows.predecessor_obligation: W05 contrasts Euclidean and Minkowski reality: the Euclidean twistor real structure acts on PT itself and preserves the CP1 fibers, while the Minkowski reality structure naturally maps PT to its dual and interchanges spinor chirality.  W05 additionally says the usual and twistor maps rho,rho_tw are the only two inequivalent real structures on CP3 in the declared scope. The linear action of SL(2,C) on C2 induces a conformal action on CP1 not commuting with its real structure; the SL(2,H)=Spin(5,1) action on C4=H2 similarly induces a CP3 action not commuting with rho_tw. Minkowski points of Gr(2,4,C) require a different real structure that maps PT=CP3 to its projective dual PT*, whereas Euclidean rho_tw acts on PT itself; the Minkowski relation exchanges the two spinor chiralities.

rows.reviewed_claim_types: R4×CP1 holomorphic fibration, quaternionic unit-sphere complex structure, Pauli +1 eigenline O(1) 2d copies
rows.predecessor_obligation: W05 gives the noncompact Euclidean twistor space R4 x CP1 the complex structure determined fiberwise by the selected orthogonal complex structure and identifies the holomorphic fibration with O(1) direct-sum O(1); for quaternionic dimension d this becomes 2d copies of O(1).  W05 gives orthogonal complex structures on R4=H by the unit imaginary quaternion x1i+x2j+x3k with x=(x1,x2,x3) a unit vector; these structures form a CP1 sphere. The map pi:R4 x CP1 -> CP1 is projection to the second factor; the total space carries the complex structure selected on R4 by the CP1 coordinate and the usual one on CP1, making pi holomorphic. Its real structure is identity on R4 and rho_tw on CP1. The holomorphic bundle is O(1) direct-sum O(1). W05 provides a separate construction using the matrices x1 sigma1+x2 sigma2+x3 sigma3 for x unit: the +1 eigenspace of this matrix on C2 above each x yields O(1). Two such copies yield O(1) direct-sum O(1) with total space R4 x CP1 and fiber R4 identified with C direct-sum C=C2, generalized to a quaternionic vector space of dimension d as 2d copies of O(1). W05 also gives the correspondence between self-dual Yang-Mills connections on S4 and holomorphic bundle structures on CP3 and describes the self-dual Einstein/nonlinear-graviton extension.

rows.reviewed_claim_types: hyperkähler aI+bJ+cK, IJ=K, dimensional reductions 1/2/3 directions and citation scope
rows.predecessor_obligation: W05 records the hyperkahler generalization as a sphere aI+bJ+cK of compatible complex/Kahler structures and relates the corresponding twistor spaces to hyperkahler quotients and moduli spaces generated from self-dual Yang-Mills and its dimensional reductions.  W05's source-given hyperkahler carrier is a manifold M of real dimension 4k with three compatible Kahler structures I,J,K obeying IJ=K and a sphere of combinations aI+bJ+cK for (a,b,c) on the unit sphere in R3. Examples include H^k, complex Lie-group coadjoint orbits, flat GL(n,C) connection moduli and Higgs-bundle moduli on a Riemann surface. Hyperkahler quotient by group G generalizes symplectic reduction; self-dual Yang-Mills connections on R4 modulo gauge transformations produce finite-dimensional moduli. Invariance in one direction yields monopoles/Bogomolny solutions, in two directions Higgs/Hitchin solutions, and in three directions complex coadjoint orbits/Nahm solutions. These are source-mentioned constructions, not qualified internal definitions.

rows.reviewed_claim_types: Hodge strict i>p, H(p,q)=Fp∩barFq, printed F²=V, mixed Hodge excluded, U1/bundle table
rows.predecessor_obligation: W05 presents Simpson's twistor-structure description of a pure real Hodge structure as a U(1)-equivariant holomorphic bundle on the twistor P1, with bundle degree/slope and the U(1) weights encoding the Hodge filtration.  W05 writes the Hodge decomposition H^n(M,C)=directsum_(p+q=n) H^(p,q)(M) and source-printed pure real weight-w Hodge filtration F^p with conjugate-complement condition F^p directsum conjugate(F^(n-p+1))=V. Its CP1 holomorphic bundle classification uses direct sums of line bundles O(w), while the twistor-real counterparts have rank two for odd degree w and rank one for even w, denoted O_(P1_tw)(w/2) with slope w/2. For V of dimension n the pure twistor E is a direct sum of n copies of O_(P1_tw)(w/2) and Hodge filtration corresponds to a U(1) action on E. W05 uses the coordinate lambda=1/z near infinity, the trivial E1=V tensor_R O_(P1_tw) away from lambda=0, and gluing with an E2 near lambda=0 using F^p. Conversely the U(1) weight spaces at lambda=0 recover the associated graded of F^p. W05's table separately pairs real Hodge structure with U(1)-equivariant twistor bundle; weight w with O_(P1_tw)(w/2) sums; underlying V with E1; and filtration with modification of E1 at infinity. These source formulas and ordered correspondences are not asserted as arbitrary lower module laws. W05 also states that although the Hodge decomposition does not vary holomorphically with changing complex structure, its filtration does. The printed decreasing-filtration chain begins 0 subset F^n subset F^(n-1) subset ... subset F^1 and concludes with an F^2=V symbol as actually printed; this unusual terminal superscript is conserved as source text without silently substituting a conventional filtration bound or claiming internal consistency. The explicit source complement is F^p directsum conjugate(F^(n-p+1))=V, and the source-printed formula gives F^p as the direct sum of H^q(M,Omega^i) over i STRICTLY GREATER than p (i>p), not i>=p; the source also prints H^(p,q)(M) = F^p intersect conjugate(F^q) under that same Hodge paragraph; the source also states the mixed Hodge case is excluded here.

W05 also defines for x=n/m in Q the p-adic norm |x|_p=p^(-a), where a is the p-power in its factorization; Qp is the completion with respect to |.|_p and R the infinite-prime completion. Over a field F the generalized quaternion algebra has basis 1,i,j,k and printed relations ij=-ji=k, i^2=a, j^2=b, for invertible a,b, denoted (a,b/F). rows.reviewed_claim_types: quaternion-conic association, Hilbert +- rational-point polarity, K-extension Galois fixedpoint free analogy
rows.predecessor_obligation: W05 associates quaternion-algebra classes with projective conics and uses the no-F-rational-point/fixed-point-free Galois action as the finite-prime analogue of the twistor P1 antipodal real structure.  W05 associates to (a,b/F) the conic C={(x,y,z): -a x^2-b y^2+ab z^2=0}. The source states that C has F-points when Hilbert symbol (a,b)_F=+1 and none when it is -1. The real H conic x^2+y^2+z^2=0 has no nonzero real solutions but has complex projective points, presenting CP1 in CP2. At a finite prime p the source gives the conic -p x^2-u y^2+up z^2=0, with no Qp points but with points over quadratic extensions K. It writes Gal(K/Qp)=Z/2Z and says this group acts on the extension-points without fixed points; the comparison to rho_tw antipodal behavior is explicitly an analogy, not source-asserted equality of systems.
